text:
maria_sales: Heads-up — customer (large telco) is asking about an on‑prem air‑gapped POC. They need: offline bundle, signed artifacts, monthly vs quarterly upgrade cadence options, and procurement/installation windows. Can we confirm constraints and pricing impact?

sam_se: Quick Qs — do they require USB/sneakernet-only delivery or can we support a controlled jumpbox (temporary egress window)?

maria_sales: They prefer sneekernet for initial install, jumpbox may be allowed for patching but legal needs to sign off. Also asking about SBOM and image signing.

devon_infra: For packaging: we recommend a small base bundle + delta patch bundles. Chunk bundles to <= 4GB for easier USB transfers. Use cosign/PKI signing and include SBOM (CycloneDX).

devon_infra: Patch cadence options: monthly security-only deltas or quarterly feature deltas. Monthly increases ops overhead and tix for onprem support; quarterly is safer for offline clients.

kevin_sec: Security notes: must deliver signed artifacts + verification instructions. We need an HSM-backed signing key on our side; customer will verify using our public cert. Cert rotation cadence must be documented. Also include clear guidance for offline cert pinning and root CA fingerprint.

maria_sales: Is there any extra compliance/legal item we should include in SOW?

lisa_cs: Yes — include offline acceptance criteria, rollback steps, and a 48–72h support SLA for POC window. This affects price: add a one‑time airgap packaging fee + optional oncall days. I can pull numbers.

sam_se: Operational checklist snippet to include for install runbook:
```
1) Verify SHA256: sha256sum bundle.tar.gz
2) Verify signature: cosign verify --key redwood.pub bundle.tar.gz
3) Unpack on isolated host, run ./install.sh --airgap
```

devon_infra: Also recommend an image provenance file: git commit hash, build date, builder image, CVE baseline. We can auto-generate during release.

kevin_sec: Firewall notes: customer asked if any IPs need to be whitelisted. For pure airgap none are required, but if they allow jumpbox patching we supply a minimal egress list and short-lived pre-signed tokens for the pull step. Documented in the runbook.

maria_sales: Customer also asked about license activation offline — do we support license files or do they need oncall activation?

lisa_cs: We support static license files (signed) plus a manual activation flow. If they want dynamic metering/usage analytics that's a separate connector (requires egress).

devon_infra: Bootstrapping approach: a detached installer (bundle + detached-operator) that performs local entitlement checks and writes local KV. For upgrades: agent enforces compatibility and will reject mismatched operator versions, we should include upgrade matrix.

kevin_sec: One more: telemetry/opt-out — ensure telemetry defaults to off and any audit logs are stored locally. Provide a short security questionnaire answer blob.

maria_sales: Perfect — can each of you drop a one‑pager (packaging + security + pricing) by EOD? I need to send to procurement to keep the deal moving.

ops_bot: Checklist created: https://redwood.workspace/checklists/edge-airgap-poc (auto-generated) :white_check_mark:

sam_se: I’ll draft the packaging one‑pager.

devon_infra: I’ll add the upgrade matrix + install runbook sections.

kevin_sec: I’ll prepare concise secQA answers and signing/cert details.

lisa_cs: I’ll attach a preliminary quote and SOW addendum.

maria_sales: Thanks team — will loop back with procurement window and customer preferred install dates. :pray:
